To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
50 % of our EROS are starbursts with SFR > 12 M⊙ yr−1 and 50 % are old early type galaxies with no star formation.
50 + 6% of the EROs are dusty starbursts, and the rest are old early type galaxies.

(1) ∼50% of our EROS sample have measureable flux at 24 μm; (2) the fraction of dusty starbursters in the EROs is 50 ±6%; (3) 20% of the EROs have a 24 μm counterpart that is not detected in the optical, and (4) ∼30% of the EROS are early type galaxies at z ∽ 1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the formation of massive early-type galaxies at high redshifts.
the formation and assembly of galaxies at high redshifts, and is based on the Spitzer observations of the FLS, the largest extragalactic Spitzer Legacy program.
the study of the most massive galaxies in the Universe, which are believed to form the bulk of the stellar mass density at z < 3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our ERO sample is a mixture of two distinct populations: 50% are star-forming dusty galaxies at 1 < z < 2.5, and 50% are massive old elliptical galaxies at z ∞ 1.5.
the ERO population is dominated by massive, old galaxies, but a substantial fraction of the ERO population are dusty starbursts, which will evolve into massive early type galaxies in a few Gyrs.
our EROs are the progenitors of massive ellipticals at z ∽ 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of the ERO population at z ∾ 1 is dominated by old, passive galaxies with a small contribution from dusty starbursts.
the optical/near-ir selected extremely red galaxies are a heterogeneous sample of dusty starburts and old early type systems at z ∽ 1, with the dusty starburst ERO fraction at 50%.
the EROs are the progenitors of the present-day massive ellipticals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EROs are a heterogeneous population, including both massive early type galaxies and dusty starburst galaxies.
the 24 μm data have revealed the presence of dusty starburts that are not seen in the optical/near-ir data, and thus, optical/near- IR selected extremely red galaxies are not all early type galaxies.
a significant fraction of the most massive early type galaxies in the local universe were formed at z ∈ 1–2 through the merging of dusty starburst galaxies.
